response.title: Preserve credential intent before applying fallback
response.summary: First establish which credential sources are authoritative, ordered, or eligible for fallback; then enforce that contract at the authentication boundary. Deliberately selected sources must not be overridden by lower-priority ambient credentials, while non-authoritative or unusable sources must not prevent supported fallbacks from being attempted.
when_to_use: Multiple credential sources can coexist and the current implementation loses their provenance, priority, or fallback relationship before authentication.
A deliberate credential selection can be overridden by ambient credentials that the downstream client treats as higher priority.
The first readable credential can be invalid, expired, or revoked while a later configured credential remains usable.
A missing explicit credential may permit an ambient path only under a narrowly observable eligibility contract.
anti_goals: Do not treat all credential sources as interchangeable merely because they can authenticate the same client.
Do not silently bypass a declared or deliberately selected credential source with ambient credentials.
Do not disable valid ambient or secondary fallback when no authoritative source excludes it.
Do not equate successful loading or parsing with successful authentication.
Do not reorder unrelated explicit overrides or redesign downstream interactive, compute, bearer-token, routing, or persistence behavior.
not_applicable_when: Only one credential source can exist and no supported fallback or precedence conflict is possible.
The intended policy is to fail closed on the first configured source rather than attempt a lower-priority source.
Source provenance cannot be retained until the authentication decision is made.
There is no safe validation oracle for determining whether a candidate credential is usable.
The defect concerns endpoint routing, token refresh, credential persistence, or provider selection rather than source authority, precedence, or fallback.
